I read the whole file. I also read the similar joint-representative integrability lemma `integrable_jointRep_restrict_prod` in ForcedRegularisedJointRep.lean, lines 219-243. Under this rubric I found no repetition that justifies a shared lemma.

The three joint square-integrability facts `hYint`, `hFint` and `hHint` already go through the single lemma `integrable_sq_jointRep_prod`. The remaining repeats are short:
- the `integral_congr_ae` / `filter_upwards [hrep…] with ξ hξ; rw [hξ]` representative-swap step;
- `pow_le_pow_left₀ (norm_nonneg _) … 2` squaring of norm bounds;
- the near-duplicate steps in `hA`, `hYt`, `hD`, `hS` and `hHt`. These differ in integrand and in how the identity is closed (`rfl`, `inner_map_map`, `Fubini`).

Pulling any of these into a helper would only move duplicated branches or wrap one-line API calls, which the rubric excludes.

The `integrable_prod_iff'` argument in `integrable_sq_jointRep_prod` resembles the one in `integrable_jointRep_restrict_prod`. That one works with L¹ norms, a finite-measure restriction on the x-side, and the Hölder bound `setIntegral_norm_le_sqrt_measure_mul_norm`. The target lemma uses squared L² norms with a pointwise-in-time bound. A unifying lemma would be non-trivial and I could not justify it with concrete rewritten uses, so I did not report it.

Remaining uncertainty: I did not search the whole repository for other copies of the square-integrability argument.
